item.text:
{
  "schema_version": "formalization-faithfulness-1",
  "role": "blind-translation",
  "dossier_sha256": "d93f2407b2ed7607f718f79043623527383f94c610a42536c83d7aecf6e788da",
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "id": "D001",
      "name": "LocalDef001",
      "meaning": "The directional update U(d,t,u)(c) = u(c) − (t/V(c)) • N(d,t,u)(c), where V is the supplied volume and N is LocalDef002.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the selected stage update appearing in the composition, cell balance, finite-segment balance, and line-agreement conclusions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "LocalDef002",
      "meaning": "N(d,t,u)(c) = F(d,t,u)(c[d := c(d)+1]) − F(d,t,u)(c), with F defined by LocalDef003.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the signed flux difference as the value at the next integer coordinate minus the value at the current coordinate.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "LocalDef003",
      "meaning": "F(d,t,u)(c) = rule(d,c,t,j ↦ u(c[d := j])).",
      "effect_on_target": "The rule receives the direction, full cell index, duration, and entire integer-indexed state line through that cell. These values supply both boundary terms and the cell flux difference.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D004",
      "name": "LocalDef004",
      "meaning": "Maps every stage (d,t) to its update U(d,t,·), then applies these updates to the initial state in list order.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the full evolution and the intermediate state obtained after the prefix before the selected stage.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D005",
      "name": "LocalDef005",
      "meaning": "Given real t and v and vectors a and f, returns a − (t/v) • f.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the exact update formula, including division by the individual cell volume and subtraction of the scaled flux difference.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "LocalDef006",
      "meaning": "Applies a finite list of state transformations from left to right, starting with the supplied state.",
      "effect_on_target": "Determines that the first listed stage acts first and that an empty stage list acts as the identity.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "AddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "An abelian additive group structure, with zero, addition, additive inverses, and subtraction.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the algebra on E needed for differences and finite sums; no order or norm on E is assumed.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D008",
      "name": "AddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid",
      "meaning": "Retains the commutative additive monoid underlying an abelian group.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the additive structure used by the module and finite sums, with the same addition and zero as E.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D009",
      "name": "AddCommGroup.toAddGroup",
      "meaning": "Retains the additive group underlying an abelian additive group.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the inherited group operations used throughout the expressions in E.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D010",
      "name": "AddGroup.toSubNegMonoid",
      "meaning": "Retains the additive monoid, negation, and subtraction structure of an additive group.",
      "effect_on_target": "Connects subtraction and the underlying additive operations to the supplied group structure on E.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D011",
      "name": "AddMonoid.toAddZeroClass",
      "meaning": "Retains addition, zero, and their identity laws from an additive monoid.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the additive zero structure used in constructing scalar multiplication instances on E.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D012",
      "name": "AddZero.toZero",
      "meaning": "Extracts the zero element from an addition-with-zero structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Identifies the zero of E used in the inherited scalar action.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D013",
      "name": "AddZeroClass.toAddZero",
      "meaning": "Retains addition and zero while forgetting the explicitly stored identity laws.",
      "effect_on_target": "Preserves the supplied additive operations while exposing the zero needed by scalar-action instances.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D014",
      "name": "And",
      "meaning": "Logical conjunction.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires all three repeated schedule properties and all four properties at every selected stage simultaneously.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D015",
      "name": "DecidableEq",
      "meaning": "For every pair of elements of D, a decision whether they are equal.",
      "effect_on_target": "Allows coordinate replacement in functions D → Z. It does not itself require D to be finite or inhabited.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D016",
      "name": "DistribMulAction.toDistribSMul",
      "meaning": "Extracts scalar multiplication preserving addition and zero from a distributive multiplicative action.",
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures that scalar multiplication in the target is inherited from the given real module structure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D017",
      "name": "DistribSMul.toSMulZeroClass",
      "meaning": "Retains scalar multiplication and its preservation of zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Forms part of the instance chain exposing the module's scalar multiplication on E.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D018",
      "name": "Eq",
      "meaning": "Equality of two objects of the same type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses exact list decomposition, equality of entire evolved states, and exact vector equalities; none of these is approximate equality.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D019",
      "name": "Exists",
      "meaning": "Existence of a witness satisfying the stated predicate.",
      "effect_on_target": "For each direction d, requires some real duration t with (d,t) in the stage list. The witness may depend on d and need not be unique.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D020",
      "name": "Finset.range",
      "meaning": "The finite set of natural numbers 0 through n−1.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes each segment sum contain exactly count terms, with no term at index count.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D021",
      "name": "Finset.sum",
      "meaning": "The sum of a function over a finite set in a commutative additive monoid.",
      "effect_on_target": "Forms volume-weighted sums in E; the sum over an empty range is zero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D022",
      "name": "Function.update",
      "meaning": "Replaces a function's value at one specified argument and leaves every other value unchanged.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines cells on a coordinate line and the next cell in the selected direction without changing any other coordinate.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D023",
      "name": "HAdd.hAdd",
      "meaning": "Extracts the addition operation from the selected heterogeneous-addition instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Here it is integer addition, used for the unit forward shift and segment coordinates.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D024",
      "name": "HAppend.hAppend",
      "meaning": "Extracts the append operation from its instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Here it concatenates the prefix with the selected stage followed by the suffix, preserving order.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D025",
      "name": "HSMul.hSMul",
      "meaning": "Extracts scalar multiplication from its instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Here real numbers act on E; volumes and durations multiply vectors by scalar action rather than by an assumed multiplication on E.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D026",
      "name": "HSub.hSub",
      "meaning": "Extracts subtraction from its instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Here it is subtraction in E, fixing the signs of updates and flux balances.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D027",
      "name": "Int",
      "meaning": "The integers Z.",
      "effect_on_target": "Cell coordinates, line indices, and segment starting indices range over all integers, including negative integers.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D028",
      "name": "Int.instAdd",
      "meaning": "The integer addition instance using Int.add.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes coordinate increments ordinary integer addition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D029",
      "name": "LT.lt",
      "meaning": "Extracts the strict comparison relation from an order instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Here it expresses strict positivity of real volumes and stage durations.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D030",
      "name": "List",
      "meaning": "Finite ordered sequences, allowing repeated entries.",
      "effect_on_target": "The schedule has finite length, its order controls execution, and repeated directions or stages are permitted.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D031",
      "name": "List.cons",
      "meaning": "Prepends one element to a list.",
      "effect_on_target": "Places the selected stage immediately before the suffix in the schedule decomposition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D032",
      "name": "List.instAppend",
      "meaning": "The list append instance, implemented by list concatenation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets schedule decomposition as ordered concatenation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D033",
      "name": "List.instMembership",
      "meaning": "List membership: an element occurs somewhere in the list.",
      "effect_on_target": "Coverage and positivity concern actual stage entries, without imposing uniqueness of occurrence.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D034",
      "name": "List.nil",
      "meaning": "The empty list.",
      "effect_on_target": "Is the list excluded by the nonemptiness hypothesis and repeated conclusion; prefixes and suffixes may still be empty.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D035",
      "name": "Membership.mem",
      "meaning": "Extracts a membership predicate, taking the collection and then the element.",
      "effect_on_target": "In this target it means that a stage pair belongs to the supplied list.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D036",
      "name": "Module",
      "meaning": "A scalar action of a semiring on an additive commutative monoid satisfying the module laws.",
      "effect_on_target": "With the scalar field R and the additive group E, makes E a real vector space, without a dimension, norm, topology, or order assumption.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D037",
      "name": "Module.toDistribMulAction",
      "meaning": "Extracts the distributive multiplicative scalar action underlying a module.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the action from which all displayed real scalar multiplications on E are obtained.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D038",
      "name": "Nat",
      "meaning": "The nonnegative integers.",
      "effect_on_target": "The segment length count and summation indices are natural numbers, and count may be zero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D039",
      "name": "Nat.cast",
      "meaning": "Applies the natural-number cast supplied by the target type's instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Here it embeds count and each summation index into Z before addition to the integer start.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D040",
      "name": "Ne",
      "meaning": "Negation of equality.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires that the stage list differ from the empty list.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D041",
      "name": "OfNat.ofNat",
      "meaning": "Interprets a natural-number numeral using the specified type's numeral instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "In the explicit target it provides the real zero used in positivity comparisons.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D042",
      "name": "Prod",
      "meaning": "The Cartesian product type of ordered pairs.",
      "effect_on_target": "A stage consists of a direction in D and a real duration.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D043",
      "name": "Prod.mk",
      "meaning": "Constructs an ordered pair from its first and second components.",
      "effect_on_target": "Builds the stage (d,t) used in coverage and schedule decomposition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D044",
      "name": "Prod.snd",
      "meaning": "Returns the second component of an ordered pair.",
      "effect_on_target": "Selects the duration whose strict positivity is assumed and repeated in the conclusion.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D045",
      "name": "Real",
      "meaning": "The real numbers R.",
      "effect_on_target": "Volumes, durations, and scalars are real-valued.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D046",
      "name": "Real.instLT",
      "meaning": "The real strict-order instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the hypotheses V(c)>0 and t>0 ordinary strict real inequalities.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D047",
      "name": "Real.instMonoid",
      "meaning": "The multiplicative monoid structure of the real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the scalar multiplication-composition structure used by the real module action and real division structure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D048",
      "name": "Real.instZero",
      "meaning": "The zero element of the real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the reference value in both positivity assumptions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D049",
      "name": "Real.semiring",
      "meaning": "The usual semiring structure on the real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the real scalar addition, multiplication, zero, and one underlying Module Real E.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D050",
      "name": "SMulZeroClass.toSMul",
      "meaning": "Extracts scalar multiplication from a scalar action preserving zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Exposes the supplied module's scalar multiplication for the weighted vectors in the target.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D051",
      "name": "SubNegMonoid.toAddMonoid",
      "meaning": "Retains the additive monoid underlying a structure with subtraction and negation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the same addition and zero of E to the scalar-action instance chain.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D052",
      "name": "SubNegMonoid.toSub",
      "meaning": "Extracts the subtraction operation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the subtraction in E used in the update and both balance identities.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D053",
      "name": "Zero.toOfNat0",
      "meaning": "Interprets the numeral zero as the zero supplied by a Zero instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures the displayed zero in the positivity predicates is real zero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D054",
      "name": "instHAdd",
      "meaning": "Uses ordinary addition as a homogeneous instance of heterogeneous addition.",
      "effect_on_target": "Resolves the displayed coordinate additions to integer addition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D055",
      "name": "instHAppendOfAppend",
      "meaning": "Uses an ordinary append operation as a homogeneous heterogeneous-append instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Resolves the schedule's append notation to list concatenation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D056",
      "name": "instHSMul",
      "meaning": "Exposes an ordinary scalar action through heterogeneous scalar-multiplication notation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Resolves all displayed scalar products to the real action on E.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D057",
      "name": "instHSub",
      "meaning": "Exposes ordinary subtraction through heterogeneous-subtraction notation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Resolves the displayed differences to subtraction in E.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D058",
      "name": "instNatCastInt",
      "meaning": "Embeds a natural number n into the integer Int.ofNat n.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the segment offsets and endpoint offset nonnegative integer copies of their natural-number indices.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D059",
      "name": "List.map",
      "meaning": "Applies a function to each list entry, preserving order and multiplicity.",
      "effect_on_target": "Converts the schedule into its corresponding sequence of directional update operators without reordering or removing repetitions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D060",
      "name": "Prod.fst",
      "meaning": "Returns the first component of an ordered pair.",
      "effect_on_target": "Selects each stage's direction when constructing its update operator.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D061",
      "name": "instOfNat",
      "meaning": "Interprets a natural-number numeral as its nonnegative integer value.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the forward coordinate increment in LocalDef002 exactly the integer one.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D062",
      "name": "DivInvMonoid.toDiv",
      "meaning": "Extracts division from a multiplication-and-inversion structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the real division used for duration divided by cell volume.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D063",
      "name": "HDiv.hDiv",
      "meaning": "Extracts division from its heterogeneous-division instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Here it is the real quotient t/V(c) in the update formula.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D064",
      "name": "List.foldl",
      "meaning": "Starting with an accumulator, successively replaces it by f(accumulator,entry) while traversing the list from first to last; an empty list returns the initial accumulator.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the evolution a sequential application of stages using the state produced by each preceding stage.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D065",
      "name": "Real.instDivInvMonoid",
      "meaning": "The real multiplicative structure with inversion and division, with division equal to multiplication by the inverse.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the quotient in the update as ordinary real division; the strictly positive volume hypothesis excludes a zero denominator in this proposition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D066",
      "name": "instHDiv",
      "meaning": "Exposes ordinary division through heterogeneous-division notation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Resolves the update coefficient to real division with numerator duration and denominator cell volume.",
      "status": "understood"
    }
  ],
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "Universally quantify a type D of coordinate directions, with decidable equality, and a type E equipped with an abelian additive group structure and a real module structure.",
      "Write C = D → Z for the set of cells. Universally quantify V : C → R.",
      "Universally quantify rule : D → C → R → (Z → E) → E and a finite ordered list S of pairs in D × R.",
      "Universally quantify the initial state u₀ : C → E.",
      "Within the conclusion, universally quantify finite lists B and A of stages, a direction d ∈ D, and a real t, subject to S = B ++ [(d,t)] ++ A. Define u = T(B,u₀), so u depends on V, rule, B, and u₀.",
      "For each such decomposition, the cell balance quantifies every c ∈ C; the segment balance quantifies every base b ∈ C, start s ∈ Z, and length n ∈ N.",
      "For each such decomposition, the line-agreement assertion quantifies every other state v : C → E and base b ∈ C, and then every integer j."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "For every cell c ∈ C, V(c) > 0.",
      "S is not the empty list.",
      "For every direction d ∈ D, there exists a real t such that (d,t) occurs in S. This witness may depend on d.",
      "Every stage (d,t) occurring in S has t > 0.",
      "The conclusions concerning a selected stage are conditional on the exact list equality S = B ++ [(d,t)] ++ A.",
      "The line-agreement conclusion is conditional on u(b[d := j]) = v(b[d := j]) for every j ∈ Z."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "The list S is nonempty, every direction occurs in S with some real duration, and every occurring stage has strictly positive duration. These three conclusions repeat the corresponding hypotheses.",
      "For every decomposition S = B ++ [(d,t)] ++ A, with u = T(B,u₀), the full evolved state satisfies T(S,u₀) = T(A,U(d,t,u)) as an equality of functions C → E.",
      "For every such decomposition and every cell c, V(c) • U(d,t,u)(c) = V(c) • u(c) − t • N(d,t,u)(c).",
      "For every such decomposition, every base b, every integer s, and every natural n, put c_k = b[d := s+k], interpreting k as an integer. Then Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} V(c_k) • U(d,t,u)(c_k) = Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} V(c_k) • u(c_k) − t • (F(d,t,u)(b[d := s+n]) − F(d,t,u)(b[d := s])).",
      "For every such decomposition, every other state v, and every base b, if u and v agree at b[d := j] for all integers j, then U(d,t,u) and U(d,t,v) agree at b[d := j] for all integers j."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "For c ∈ C, c[d := j] denotes the cell whose coordinate at d is j and whose other coordinates equal those of c. The unit forward shift is c⁺ᵈ = c[d := c(d)+1].",
      "The symbol • denotes the given real scalar multiplication on E. All vector differences and finite sums use E's abelian additive group operations.",
      "F(d,t,u)(c) = rule(d,c,t,j ↦ u(c[d := j])). Thus the rule's state argument is the entire line indexed by absolute integer coordinate j, while c remains a separate argument.",
      "N(d,t,u)(c) = F(d,t,u)(c⁺ᵈ) − F(d,t,u)(c).",
      "U(d,t,u)(c) = u(c) − (t/V(c)) • N(d,t,u)(c). The same V and rule are used in every occurrence of U, F, N, and T.",
      "T([],u) = u, and T((d,t)::L,u) = T(L,U(d,t,u)). Consequently, for S = [(d₁,t₁),…,(d_m,t_m)], T(S,u₀) is obtained by applying these updates in the listed order, each to the state produced by its predecessors.",
      "Each finite-segment sum runs over natural indices k with 0 ≤ k < n. Its cells have direction-d coordinates s through s+n−1, and its two flux evaluations have direction-d coordinates s and s+n."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For any real vector space E, any direction type D with decidable equality, any strictly positive real volume assigned to every integer-coordinate cell, and any rule assigning an E-valued result from a direction, cell, real duration, and complete state line, consider a nonempty finite ordered schedule of positive-duration directional stages covering every direction. For every initial state, the schedule retains those three stated properties. At every occurrence of a stage in the schedule, let the current state be the result of applying the preceding stages. The final state is exactly the result of applying that stage to the current state and then applying the remaining stages. At each cell, this stage changes the volume-weighted state by minus the duration times the forward difference of the rule-defined flux. On every finite consecutive segment in that direction, these changes sum to minus the duration times the terminal flux minus the initial flux. Finally, if another state agrees with the current state along an entire line in the selected direction, the two states also agree along that line after applying the same selected stage."
  },
  "restrictions_and_vacuity_risks": [
    "Although D is not explicitly equipped with a finiteness or nonemptiness instance, a finite schedule covering all directions forces D to have finitely many elements, and a nonempty list of pairs in D × R forces D to be inhabited. For infinite or empty D, the schedule hypotheses cannot all hold, so the implication is vacuous.",
    "Coverage requires at least one stage per direction. It does not require exactly one stage per direction, distinct stage pairs, equal durations, a prescribed order, or a prescribed total duration.",
    "The direction and duration in the stage-specific conclusion must arise from a decomposition of the given schedule. For tuples that do not give that decomposition, the conditional assertion imposes no requirement.",
    "The volume is strictly positive at every cell, not merely at cells in a selected segment. It may vary arbitrarily with the cell; no uniform lower bound or geometric interpretation is assumed.",
    "Cells comprise all functions D → Z, and states are arbitrary functions on all these cells. There are no spatial boundary restrictions, periodicity assumptions, finite-support conditions, or summability assumptions.",
    "The segment length may be zero. In that case both sums are zero and the two endpoint flux evaluations coincide, so the segment identity is trivial.",
    "The rule is arbitrary and may depend on the full cell index, direction, duration, and entire state line. No finite stencil, continuity, linearity, consistency with a differential equation, stability, or positivity preservation is encoded.",
    "The line-agreement conclusion concerns one selected directional update using the same volume and rule. It requires agreement on the entire integer line and does not assert locality to a finite neighborhood or preservation of line agreement by the full schedule.",
    "The finite-segment balance includes a boundary-flux difference. It does not assert that the segment's weighted sum remains unchanged, or that a total sum over the full grid exists or is conserved.",
    "E need not be finite-dimensional, normed, ordered, or nontrivial. In the zero vector space the vector equalities hold trivially, while the schedule and volume hypotheses remain required.",
    "The first three conclusions restate assumptions. The proposition does not construct a covering schedule or prove positive durations from properties of the update.",
    "The words cell volume, state, duration, and flux describe argument roles; the declaration does not supply geometric cells, physical units, a time-dependent physical solution, or an accuracy or convergence claim."
  ],
  "ambiguities": []
}
